question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Jouvian, however, having quitted the water, sought in every possible direction for his horse and clothes.

A. “Miserable that I am,” said he, “to what a strait am I reduced!”

B. I will then ride on to the palace and strictly investigate the cause of this extraordinary conduct.

C. There is, I remember, a knight who lives close by; I will go to him and command his attendance and service.

D. Vexed beyond measure at the circumstance (for he was completely naked and saw no one near to assist him), he began to reflect upon what course he should pursue.

S2: Some shall smart for it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Distress at the situation, an exclamation, then a plan of action.

• D (his reaction to not finding his things, described in S1) → A (his exclamation, continuing the reflection begun in D) → C (a plan he arrives at, following his exclamation of misery in A) → B (‘then’ continues the plan from C, the next step)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘I will then...’ continues a plan only after the first step of that plan has been stated.

 

NOTE

• B's ‘then’ continues directly from the first step of the plan stated in C, so C must precede B.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: From beyond the sea came hosts of Greeks, armed for war and bent upon the conquest of the city.

A. They cried for vengeance, and heroes and warriors from every city of that country joined hands and vowed vengeance upon Troy.

B. He had stolen and carried away from her shores the most beautiful of all her women, even Helen, the wife of Menelaus of Sparta.

C. They came in a thousand little ships, with sails and oars, and landed on the beach at the foot of the plain.

D. They came because one of the princes of Troy, Paris by name, had done a grievous wrong to Greece.

S2: They built huts and tents along the shore; they kindled fires; they threw up a breastwork of earth and stones around their camp; they defied the warriors of Troy to come out on the plain and meet them in battle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, B, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The cause of the war, the Greeks' vow, then their arrival.

• D (explains why the Greeks came, named in S1 — Paris's wrong) → B (‘He’ is Paris from D, explaining the ‘grievous wrong’ — stealing Helen) → A (the Greeks' (‘They’) reaction — vowing vengeance — to the wrong described in B) → C (describes the actual arrival, following the vow of vengeance in A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A pronoun like ‘He’ needs a specific named person introduced immediately before.

 

NOTE

• B's ‘He’ refers to Paris named only in D, so D must precede B.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: As for Simmons, however, he was held fortunate in that capable wife.

A. Nobody could tell what might not have happened to Tommy Simmons if there had been no Mrs. Simmons to take care of him.

B. He had no vices (even his pipe departed him after his marriage), and Mrs. Simmons had ingrained on him divers exotic virtues.

C. He was a moderately good carpenter and joiner, but no man of the world, and he wanted to be one.

D. He was a meek and quiet man, with a boyish face and sparse, limp whiskers.

S2: He went solemnly to chapel every Sunday, under a tall hat, and put a penny—one returned to him for the purpose out of his week’s wages—in the plate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, A, D, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Simmons's own limitations, his wife's care, and its results.

• C (describes Simmons (‘He’) himself, before his wife's help is discussed) → A (introduces Mrs Simmons's role, following his own limitations described in C) → D (further describes Simmons, continuing after A's mention of him needing care) → B (describes the result of his wife's care, leading into S2's churchgoing habit)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A conditional about needing someone's care needs that person's own weaknesses already described.

 

NOTE

• A's conditional about needing his wife's care follows naturally from Simmons's own limitations already described in C.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: It was a close, musty, ill- ventilated place, as might be expected, since its inmate seldom left it.

A. A thick dark veil covered her face, but it was cut off close at her upper lip and disclosed a perfectly shaped mouth and a delicately rounded chin.

B. From keen beasts in a cage, the woman seemed by some retribution of fate to have become herself a beast in a cage.

C. She sat now in a broken armchair in the shadowy corner of the room.

D. Long years of inaction had coarsened the lines of her figure, but at some period it must have been beautiful, and was still full and voluptuous.

S2: I could well conceive that she had indeed been a very remarkable woman.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, C, D, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Introducing the confined woman, then describing her figure and face.

• B (introduces ‘the woman,’ linking her to the confined place of S1) → C (‘She’ is the woman from B, describing her position in the room) → D (continues describing her (‘her figure’), from C) → A (continues the physical description from D, moving to her face)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A person must be introduced before pronouns like ‘She’ and ‘her’ describe her further.

 

NOTE

• C, D and A all use ‘She/her’ referring to ‘the woman’ introduced only in B, so B must come first.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The two went to their business.

A. He seated himself at the matchmaker’s side but facing him, attempting by an act of will to suppress the unpleasant tickle in his throat.

B. As he flipped through them, a gesture and sound that physically hurt Leo, the student pretended not to see and gazed steadfastly out the window.

C. Salzman eagerly unstrapped his portfolio and removed a loose rubber band from a thin packet of much-handled cards.

D. Leo had led Salzman to the only clear place in the room, a table near a window that overlooked the lamp-lit city.

S2: Although it was still February, winter was on its last legs, signs of which he had for the first time in years begun to notice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A business meeting between Leo and Salzman, and the cards being handled.

• D (describes the location of ‘their business’ (S1), naming Leo and Salzman) → A (‘He’ is Leo, ‘the matchmaker’ is Salzman, continuing from D) → C (Salzman's action, following the seating in A) → B (‘them’ refers to the cards just named in C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A pronoun like ‘them’ needs its noun introduced in the sentence immediately before.

 

NOTE

• B's ‘them’ refers to the cards named only in C, so C must precede B.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: On the morning of the fourth day, while Khaled, according to his custom, rode out over the plain and passed close to the tents reserved for strangers, he caught sight of Djaida mounting her horse.

A. “Until this moment I have failed in courtesy towards you, but now I beg of you, in the name of that God who has given you such great dexterity in arms, tell me who you are, and to what noble princes are you allied?”

B. He saluted her, and she returned his salute.

C. For I have never yet met equal among brave warriors.

D. “Noble Arab,” said Khaled, “I would ask you one question.”

S2: Answer me, I beseech you, for I am most impatient to learn.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, D, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A greeting, then Khaled's request explained in his own words.

• B (a direct, immediate interaction following the sighting in S1) → D (Khaled speaks, continuing after the salute in B) → A (continues Khaled's speech, elaborating on the ‘one question’ announced in D) → C (continues Khaled's flattering speech from A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• An announcement of a coming question should precede the actual question itself.

 

NOTE

• A's detailed request only makes sense after D announces that a question is coming, so D must precede A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Miss Janet Dalrymple, daughter of the first Lord Stair and Dame Margaret Ross, had engaged herself without the knowledge of her parents to the Lord Rutherford.

A. The young lady refused the proposal and being pressed on the subject, confessed her secret engagement.

B. Shortly after, a suitor who was favoured by Lord Stair and still more so by his lady, paid his addresses to Miss Dalrymple.

C. Lady Stair insisted upon her daughter yielding her consent to marry the new suitor, David Dunbar.

D. The young couple broke a piece of gold together and pledged their troth.

S2: The first lover then interfered by letter and insisted on the right he had acquired by his troth plighted with the young lady.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, B, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A secret engagement, a rival suitor, refusal and confession, then parental pressure.

• D (describes the secret engagement act itself, from S1) → B (a new development — a rival suitor — following the secret engagement in D) → A (her reaction to the suitor introduced in B) → C (the parents' response, following the confession in A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A confession must follow both the event confessed and the pressure that provoked it.

 

NOTE

• A's confession follows the new suitor's proposal introduced in B, so B must precede A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Memon, covered with shame and confusion, got home to his own house; here he found a card inviting him to dinner with some of his intimate friends.

A. I shall forget in the sweets of their society that folly I have this morning been guilty of.

B. Accordingly, he attends the meeting; he is discovered to be uneasy at something, and he is urged to drink and banish care.

C. It will therefore be prudent in me to go to my intimate friends and partake with them of a frugal repast.

D. If I remain at home alone, said he, I shall have my mind occupied with this vexatious adventure.

S2: A little wine, drunk in moderation, comforts the heart of god and man.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, C, A, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Internal reasoning about whether to stay home, then the decision acted upon.

• D (his first thought, following S1's discovery of the invitation) → C (‘therefore’ draws the conclusion from D's reasoning) → A (continues his reasoning about going out, from C) → B (‘Accordingly’ marks the action taken as a result of the reasoning in D, C and A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Accordingly’ marks an action that follows a completed chain of reasoning, so it comes last.

 

NOTE

• B's ‘Accordingly, he attends’ is the acted-upon conclusion of the reasoning in D, C and A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: My two old gentlemen sat half in the shadow of the green lamp-shade, moldering ruins both, from long-past days.

A. One, the host, is evidently an old officer.

B. The other, who sits near him on the sofa, is a tall spare figure.

C. He sits holding the handle of his roller-like a crutch tightly clasped in both hands.

D. His pointed moustache and martial eyebrows suggest his background.

S2: Among the myriad wrinkles of his smooth-shaven face there lurked a quiet, gentle smile.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, C, D, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Describing the first of two old gentlemen fully, then introducing the second.

• A (introduces ‘One’ of the ‘two old gentlemen’ named in S1) → C (‘He’ is the host from A, continuing his description) → D (further description of the host, following C) → B (introduces ‘the other’ gentleman, paired with ‘one’ from A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘One...the other’ pairs are usually developed one at a time.

 

NOTE

• B's ‘the other’ should only appear once the first gentleman has been fully described in A, C and D.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Ash’s books were most regrettably scattered across Europe and America.

A. That was no problem nowadays, books travelled the aether like light and sound.

B. And Roland was looking for sources for Ash’s Garden of Proserpina.

C. But it was just possible that Ash’s own Wico had marginalia missed even by the indefatigable Cropper.

D. By far the largest single gathering was of course in the Stant Collection at Robert Dale Owen University in New Mexico.

S2: And there was a pleasure to be had from reading the sentences Ash had read, touched with his fingers, scanned with his eyes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Scattered book collections, ease of access, and Roland's specific research.

• D (names the largest single collection, following on from ‘scattered’ in S1) → A (comments on the ease of access (‘That’) to such distant collections) → C (‘But’ introduces a complication despite the ease described in A) → B (introduces Roland's specific search, continuing from the possibility raised in C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘But’ introduces a complication that must follow the point it complicates.

 

NOTE

• C's ‘But’ only makes sense as a complication to the ease of access claimed in A, so A must precede C.
